messages.author: a0400723101de00c
messages.subject: object 'POST' not found
parts:
Hi everyone,
Im very new to R and Rapache in particular,but its a great learning
process so far and an excellent tool.I have come across some strange
behaviour.I know I am probably mis configuring something in the
apache2 http.conf configuration file,but basically when I do a POST of
a variable to an R script under 1 configuratoin,I get an error saying
Object POST not found. Im hoping someone might be able to help me
figure out what I am doing wrong.So far google,and trial and
experimentation havent worked.
To describe abit more what I want to achieve,basically I want
REvalOnStartup to source a main .R file on startup.This .R file will
load alot of data into memory as apache starts up.Ive set up a simple
POST form that sends data to a specific URL, which will make the call
to the .R file passing a POST variable to the .R file.However when the
user hits submit,the object not found error is thrown.If I take out
the POST object,the R source is parsed,and a plot is returned.(errors
also thrown for GET,setContentType etc)
What is strange to me,is that if I create a config such as
<location /url/hello>
RFileHandler /home/pat/testRPlot.R::plotTest
</location>
Then the user is able to submit the form,and pass the variable to
the .R script which is then found and used correctly in the .R file.

Ive attached some code which reproduces my issue...Im sorry about all
the code,im sure im doing something trivial wrong,but I cannot seem to
move past this blocker.The main .R file takes over 1 min to run,so it
would not be an acceptable user experience to wait for the process to
run,each time they hit submit.Any ideas or hints would be greatfully
accepted.
Thanks in advance,

testRPlot.R
plotTest <- function(r) {

png(type="cairo","/var/www/R/images/hello7.png")
# make a very simple plot
xAxis <- c(100,3,6,9,12)
yAxis <- c(100,2,7,8,15)
plot(xAxis,yAxis)

dev.off()


cat("<html>")
cat("<body>")
cat("<h1>hello world- handler</h1>")

cat("<h1>")
cat( POST$crop ) #Depending on config,POST object not found..why?
cat(" </h1>")

cat('<img src="../R/images/hello7.png"')
cat("</body>")
cat("</html>")

}

/etc/apache2/httpd.conf
LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

Config 1:
REvalOnStartup "source('/home/pat/testRPlot.R')"

<Location /appname/hello>

SetHandler r-handler
RHandler plotTest #R code parsed,but not POST/GET/
setContentType etc

</Location>

Config 2:

<Location /appname/hello>
SetHandler r-handler
RFileHandler /home/pat/testRPlot.R::plotTest #This
works,but would be very expensive/timely to run at every request

</Location>


/var/www/testRRequest.html
<html>
<head>Rapache Test</head>
<body>
<form method="POST" action="/appname/hello">
<input type="text" name="crop" value="wheat">
<input type="text" name="country" value="USA">
<input type="submit" name="Submit">
</form>

</body>
</html>

OS:Ubuntu: 10.04
R version : 2.12
RApache version: 1.1.12

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: object 'POST' not found
parts:
Congratulations patohora, you've found a bug! Expect a new release on
the 1.1 branch in a few days.

It's a tricky one and has to do with where your function is created.
When you use the directive RSourceOnStartup, for the typical case all
of your data and functions will be defined in the global environment.
Thus as you have found out, all of the CGI variables, and even the
rApache functions, are never found. However if you use RFileHanlder
/path/to/file::function, then an anonymous environment is created that
contain your data and code and the rapache environment which contains
the CGI vars and functions are attached to it as the parent
environment. Hence, rapache is found by lexical scoping rules.

The bug is one I introduced a few versions ago. I was using some
really nasty C level environment tricks to assign the rapache
environment to the parent of each function invocation, but I decided
against that since finding out it's not really *standard R practice*.
The solution is to create a named rapache environment, stick it on the
search path, then run the user's method for each request.

Read below for a comment on your config.

Actually, the additional cost of this way of running plotTest vs. your
previous one using RSourceOnStartup is just one file stat. It's not
sourced if the modified time has not changed, so it should be pretty
fast. In fact I use this way the most in my own programming (that's
why I didn't find your bug befure). Also, the convenience of not
having to restart the web server far outweighs the cost.

Best,

Jeff
